request.system:
You are a property damage assessor examining a single photo submitted with a home insurance claim.
Describe only what is visible. You are deliberately not told the customer's story - do not guess one.

- room_type: the room or part of the building shown. Use non_residential when the setting is clearly not a
  private home (shop, museum, office, public building). Use unknown when only a ceiling/wall/detail is visible.
- image_quality: not_a_damage_photo when the photo shows no damage at all.
- damage_types: choose every type that is visible; use other only when nothing else fits.
- long_term_signs_visible: mould, rot, rust, layered tide marks, salt deposits, weathering, lichen.
- visible_text / regional_indicators: report readable street signs, plates, socket or plug types, building
  styles that hint at a country. These are recorded as observations, not accusations.
- confidence is your own estimate and is never used for decisions.

room_type_cues: wall-mounted wooden cabinet with hinges in the corner
dark appliance or surface at the bottom left
textured ceiling and wall in a residential style

damaged_parts.condition: extensive brown water stains with black mould colonies, with the surface layer peeling and collapsing
exposed, dark, degraded and apparently rotted wood where the ceiling material has fallen away
peeling and detached paint and plaster with black mould spotting along the edge
a patch of paint or texture has peeled away to expose the brown substrate beneath
cracked veneer or finish on the cabinet's top and side panel

regional_indicators: popcorn ceiling and textured walls common in North American homes
oak-style wall cabinet typical of North American builder-grade kitchens
parsed_output.summary_en: A ceiling corner above a wall cabinet shows widespread brown water staining, black mould growth and peeling textured plaster, with a section of dark, degraded timber joist exposed. The adjacent wall also shows peeled paint and mould spotting along the ceiling edge, indicating prolonged moisture exposure.
